blocks.text: The wish

content.value: Move the LiveView Studio from a functional 3/10 toward a genuinely premium editing surface — the Kinsta/Vercel/Sanity bar, where interaction feels considered, states are never blank, and the highest-traffic panes carry real visual hierarchy. The token system, themes, structure/desk tiering, and the email fleet are DONE; what remains is INTERACTION quality on the surfaces authors actually live in: the document editor, the desk/structure lists, the paper canvas, the API tester, media + sheet grids.

REJECT tree-tidiness and show-off cosmetic churn. The AI-Score finding: only naming/canonical-pointer governance measured POSITIVE — cosmetic reshuffles measured neutral-to-negative. Every slice must be a felt improvement on a high-traffic pane, not a refactor.

blocks.text: Direction — what the finished wave looks like (tentative; Decide finalizes)

content.value: North star, stated as an experience: an author opens the highest-traffic Studio pane and it feels ALIVE and considered — the editor tells you it saved, a slow load shows a skeleton not a blank, an empty desk invites the first document instead of staring back, keyboard users can drive the core loop (save, navigate fields, dismiss modals) without reaching for the mouse, and the visual hierarchy makes the primary action obvious. Nothing new is invented cosmetically; every change is a felt fix on a surface authors touch dozens of times a day.

The choices I lean toward (for Decide to confirm after two Explore rounds): concentrate 2-4 slices on the DOCUMENT EDITOR and the DESK/STRUCTURE LIST — the two panes with the most author time. Candidate slices: (a) editor save-state affordance — Saving…/Saved/Error, aria-live, so autosave is trustworthy; (b) loading/skeleton + honest error states across the high-traffic list panes where today a slow query shows blank; (c) keyboard affordances for the core loop — save shortcut, field traversal, modal Esc/focus-trap, focus-visible rings; (d) visual hierarchy pass on ONE named pane (likely the desk list or editor header) — primary action prominence, spacing rhythm, not a re-theme. Pick the 2-4 with the highest felt-improvement-per-file-touched and cleanest disjointness.

Explicit anti-goals: no re-theming (themes are done), no token-manifest churn (unified-aesthetic is done), no desk re-tiering (structure-polish is done), no email work (GUI-premium is done), no cross-pane refactor for its own sake. If Explore proves the polish is already there, we downgrade to a thin verification wave and record that honestly.

protective-test-surface — What LiveView test infrastructure exists for Studio (test/.../live/studio/*, LiveViewTest, data-test-id coverage)? Can we assert save-state / loading / keyboard behavior in a test? WHY: decides which slices get a test vs a manual recipe.

STUDIO PREMIUM OVERHAUL · CHARTER EXISTS · DIGEST (RESUMED) · VERIFYING · 2026-07-14

Studio Premium — from functional 3/10 toward a genuinely premium editing surface

CORRECTED (post spend-cap resume): this is NOT a founding wave and NOT a 3/10 greenfield. The charter .claude/workflows/bp-studio-ui-premium-charter.md (733 lines, D1-D27) IS committed on origin/main @51576f128; epic studio-ui-premium (8f096da3) has 18 children, 17 done, 1 open (sup-w4-pixel-evidence, an unrelated gated pixel reshoot). Decide AMENDS this existing charter with a wave-5 interaction-polish section — it does NOT write a new bp-studio-premium-charter.md (that forks the epic). See the RESUMED DIGEST section below; the earlier 'founding wave' blocks are kept as historical record.

The wish

Move the LiveView Studio from a functional 3/10 toward a genuinely premium editing surface — the Kinsta/Vercel/Sanity bar, where interaction feels considered, states are never blank, and the highest-traffic panes carry real visual hierarchy. The token system, themes, structure/desk tiering, and the email fleet are DONE; what remains is INTERACTION quality on the surfaces authors actually live in: the document editor, the desk/structure lists, the paper canvas, the API tester, media + sheet grids.

• GROUND TRUTH FIRST — inventory what already shipped (theme, unified-aesthetic, structure-polish, email) vs what premium gaps genuinely remain, and which remaining gaps are net-new vs already in-flight in a concurrent session. bp search first; scan open PRs + foreign claims before Decide dispatches.
• REJECT tree-tidiness and show-off cosmetic churn. The AI-Score finding: only naming/canonical-pointer governance measured POSITIVE — cosmetic reshuffles measured neutral-to-negative. Every slice must be a felt improvement on a high-traffic pane, not a refactor.
• Each slice: file-disjoint, high-leverage, with a NAMED before/after and either a protective test or a concrete live-Studio verification recipe.
• Model constraint: Fable is EXHAUSTED — every phase runs on OPUS. Builders branch from ORIGIN/main (local checkout diverged), work in isolated worktrees, COMMIT (do not push); the steward pushes green branches. Elixir gate = CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test <touched files> in an isolated partition DB.

Ground truth so far (Strategize skim — verify in Explore)

• Studio LiveView lives in api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio/ (studio_live.ex 562L is the shell; editor.ex 827L, modals.ex 981L, nav.ex 698L, panes.ex 423L, controls.ex 329L are the component surfaces). Layout: layouts/studio.html.heex. Tokens: studio/tokens_gen.ex (63L, generated from the unified manifest).
• State primitives ALREADY EXIST: empty_editor/1, pane_empty/1 (.empty-state), role="status" + aria-live="polite" on violations, ~94 phx-/aria-/keydown hits across studio_components. So this is POLISH territory, not greenfield — the surveyors must judge the QUALITY and COVERAGE of what exists, not assume absence.
• The editor form (editor.ex:439) uses phx-submit="save" + phx-change="autosave" with phx-debounce=300 — but no obvious Saving…/Saved feedback echo was seen in the skim. Classic premium gap to confirm: autosave with no save-state affordance.
• High-traffic panes ranked by author time: (1) document editor, (2) desk/structure list, (3) paper canvas, (4) API tester, (5) media grid, (6) sheet grid. Premium leverage concentrates on 1-2.
• Prior art in the ledger: the Connectors wave-4 paper already frames the 'Kinsta/Vercel bar' and shows Studio's admin list-page skeleton (PluginsLive, LiveScope.on_mount fail-closed). studio-structure-polish, theme-system, unified-aesthetic W4, GUI-premium are all logged COMPLETE in memory — treat as DONE, verify no regression only.

Direction — what the finished wave looks like (tentative; Decide finalizes)

North star, stated as an experience: an author opens the highest-traffic Studio pane and it feels ALIVE and considered — the editor tells you it saved, a slow load shows a skeleton not a blank, an empty desk invites the first document instead of staring back, keyboard users can drive the core loop (save, navigate fields, dismiss modals) without reaching for the mouse, and the visual hierarchy makes the primary action obvious. Nothing new is invented cosmetically; every change is a felt fix on a surface authors touch dozens of times a day.

The choices I lean toward (for Decide to confirm after two Explore rounds): concentrate 2-4 slices on the DOCUMENT EDITOR and the DESK/STRUCTURE LIST — the two panes with the most author time. Candidate slices: (a) editor save-state affordance — Saving…/Saved/Error, aria-live, so autosave is trustworthy; (b) loading/skeleton + honest error states across the high-traffic list panes where today a slow query shows blank; (c) keyboard affordances for the core loop — save shortcut, field traversal, modal Esc/focus-trap, focus-visible rings; (d) visual hierarchy pass on ONE named pane (likely the desk list or editor header) — primary action prominence, spacing rhythm, not a re-theme. Pick the 2-4 with the highest felt-improvement-per-file-touched and cleanest disjointness.

Explicit anti-goals: no re-theming (themes are done), no token-manifest churn (unified-aesthetic is done), no desk re-tiering (structure-polish is done), no email work (GUI-premium is done), no cross-pane refactor for its own sake. If Explore proves the polish is already there, we downgrade to a thin verification wave and record that honestly.

Survey plan — the scout questions (each becomes one Sonnet surveyor)

Width is cheap now. The survey casts a wide net across the current Studio, the shipped aesthetic systems, the ledger, and concurrent sessions; Digest distills before the verify fleet flies. Each assignment below names suspected files, claims to check, and how the answer changes the plan.

editor-state-audit — In editor.ex + studio_live.ex, is there ANY Saving…/Saved/Error feedback for autosave (phx-change=autosave)? Trace the save/autosave event handlers. WHY: the marquee candidate slice; if feedback already exists, drop it.

list-pane-loading-states — Across panes.ex, media_live.ex, sheet_grid, graph_view, api_tester_live: what shows during a slow/empty/failed load — skeleton, spinner, blank, or error? Map each high-traffic pane's three states. WHY: decides the loading/empty/error slice scope.

keyboard-affordances — Inventory phx-keydown/phx-window-keydown, tabindex, focus-trap, Esc-to-close, focus-visible across studio_components + modals.ex. What core-loop actions are mouse-only today? WHY: sizes the keyboard slice.

existing-aesthetic-inventory — What did theme-system, unified-aesthetic W4, studio-structure-polish, GUI-premium ACTUALLY ship for Studio? Read their memory notes + the commits/PRs. Draw the DONE line precisely so we don't redo it. WHY: prevents re-doing finished work.

token-system-constraints — How does tokens_gen.ex + the unified manifest work? Where do Studio CSS variables come from, and what's the sanctioned way to add spacing/hierarchy without forking tokens? WHY: any visual-hierarchy slice must ride the token system, not fork it.

concurrent-session-scan — Scan OPEN PRs (gh pr list) + foreign task claims + integrate/*, loop-epic/* branches for in-flight Studio UI work. Is anyone already polishing the editor or lists? WHY: dedupe before Decide dispatches file-disjoint slices.

ledger-studio-tasks — Search bp tasks/papers for open Studio-UI/premium/polish work: existing children, prior charters, deferred items. What's already filed vs net-new? WHY: Decide files from this; must be exact.

highest-traffic-pane-truth — Confirm which Studio panes authors actually use most (routes, nav.ex tabs, default landing). Is the document editor really #1? WHY: leverage ranking drives which panes get slices.

empty-state-quality — Read empty_editor/1 + pane_empty/1 + .empty-state CSS. Are empty states inviting (CTA, icon, guidance) or bare text? Screenshot-level judgment. WHY: empty-state quality is a cheap high-visibility premium win.

error-surface-audit — How do Studio errors reach the user today — flash, inline, silent, crash? Trace save failures, publish failures, query failures. WHY: honest error states are core to premium; find the silent-failure paths.

modal-interaction-polish — modals.ex is 981L. Do modals trap focus, close on Esc/backdrop, restore focus, animate? What's the interaction quality? WHY: modals are high-friction; sizes a possible slice.

micro-interaction-baseline — What transitions/hover/active/loading affordances exist on buttons, tabs, list rows today (CSS + phx-click-loading)? Is there any motion, or is it static? WHY: distinguishes real polish from cosmetic churn — only felt interactions count.

live-studio-verification-recipe — Can Studio be driven locally or against guerrilla for before/after verification (login gate, chrome-devtools MCP, screenshots)? What's the concrete recipe? WHY: every slice needs a live-Studio verify recipe or a protective test.

protective-test-surface — What LiveView test infrastructure exists for Studio (test/.../live/studio/*, LiveViewTest, data-test-id coverage)? Can we assert save-state / loading / keyboard behavior in a test? WHY: decides which slices get a test vs a manual recipe.

visual-hierarchy-candidates — On the editor header + desk list, judge current hierarchy: is the primary action obvious, is spacing rhythmic, does the eye land right? Name the single highest-leverage hierarchy fix. WHY: scopes the one visual-hierarchy slice without re-theming.

What happens next

Sonnet surveyors answer the questions above (coverage-accounted). Digest folds their reports into this Paper, draws the DONE line, and designs the verify fleet that PROVES the remaining-gap claims with run output. Decide then writes + commits .claude/workflows/bp-studio-premium-charter.md to origin/main, cuts 2-4 file-disjoint slices as bp tasks (each linked to this Paper), and dispatches Opus builders. This Paper is the living story — every phase appends; the debrief closes it.
